protected-rejection-the-rulings-and-what.text: Protected rejection: the rulings and what they decide.

This page records every operator ruling that governs ticket 494, in the operator's words, and the model readings that follow from them. It carries forward, unchanged in meaning, the rulings and the historical counterexample recorded for the earlier model candidate (pull request 508). Nothing here re-asks a ruling.

the-requester-story-and-the-behavior-it-.text: The requester story and the behavior it reproduces.

As a requester with an approved insertion for an unknown key, I want a permissionless processor unable to cancel it and collect its tip without an allowed rejection condition, so that paying for processing does not enable arbitrary cancellation.

The earlier candidate reproduced the defect at model revision 6efe1f119a2332484e690b4c128c4bc5fd4d689b with an empty registry and an approved insertion of key 5 for owner 42, destination 99, deposit 2,000,000 and tip 1,000,000. The insertion folds to Active. The same request can instead be rejected with no signers, unchanged registry state, no mint and a deposit-only refund to the owner, while the modelled inputs exceed the modelled outputs by the tip.

The tree this ticket starts from (e3c9ab01, the two-edge model) has the same defect: its exitAdmission answers no refusal for Exit.reject, so the same scenario is accepted. The scenario is therefore the failing control of the first coding slice that changes rejection, and it is kept as historical behavior: it is run against the base model before the change (it must report the rejection accepted) and against the changed model after it (it must report the rejection refused). It is model evidence only; it is not a ledger attack and does not prove any validator behavior.

ruling-a-lifecycle-mismatch-permits-imme.text: Ruling: a lifecycle mismatch permits immediate rejection.

The operator answered "reject" to the story of Alice active on a key and Bob requesting an insertion for it, a request that deletion could later make possible, with the processor taking the tip. The ruling, verbatim:
Authenticated incompatibility with the current lifecycle state permits immediate rejection even when a later transition could make the request eligible.

Refund amounts are unchanged by it, and it does not resolve ticket 361 (the unresolved owner-sum versus positional refund discrepancy). It does not select the state used in a mixed batch (see the third ruling), an expiry boundary (see the second), or any further reason.

ruling-expiry-follows-both-windows.text: The operator answered "yes" to expiry-only rejection after both the processing and the owner's reclaim windows end, so that the owner keeps the opportunity to reclaim the deposit and tip. The ruling, verbatim:
expiry-only rejection after both the processing and owner's reclaim windows end ... The expiry threshold is therefore submission time plus processing duration plus reclaim duration.

With submission 10000, processing duration 1000 and reclaim duration 500 the threshold is 11500. An expiry-only rejection must not execute before it: its whole validity interval lies at or after the threshold. This does not delay the separately authorized mismatch rejection of the first ruling, and refund amounts remain unchanged.

ruling-a-batch-is-judged-on-the-state-it.text: Ruling: a batch is judged on the state its earlier actions left.

On 8 October 2026 the operator answered "yes, the batching work should be closed on its effects" for two insertions of the same initially unknown key: fold the first, then reject the second against the updated state. The ruling, verbatim:
Each action is judged against the state left by preceding actions in the same ordered batch. Rejection evidence binds that intermediate registry state/root.

An earlier successful action may create the lifecycle mismatch that authorizes a later rejection. A rejection preserves the intermediate state it saw, so later actions see every earlier successful transition. This is a required mixed-batch property of the model, not a claim that a batch builder or a batch acceptance exists.

scope-confirmation.text: The operator required proof of rejectability, assigned malformed-deposit and address pollution research to ticket 500, and directed the model work to proceed. Exactly two grounds authorize rejection: a lifecycle mismatch and expiry. No other reason is authorized. A provider failure, a missing processor-supplied input, an invalid proof and a generic script failure are never evidence that a request is inadmissible.

readings-that-follow-from-the-two-edge-m.text: Readings that follow from the two-edge model.

The base model admits only registration (insertActive) and permanent termination (updateTerminal); five older edge tags remain in wire order solely to represent refused actions. Three readings follow and are recorded here so the coding slices do not choose them silently.

decision-pending-what-the-public-suite-s.text: Decision pending: what the public suite shows until the validators change.

Once the model refuses an in-window rejection of a foldable request, the required check named "early rejection inside the windows" cannot agree between model and chain, because the validators (ticket 495) still accept it. The question and its three options are in the ticket owner's question file for the epic owner; the plan marks every row that depends on it. It is not decided here.

what-is-carried-forward-unchanged-from-t.text: What is carried forward unchanged from the earlier candidate.

The earlier candidate was reviewed twice by an independent model and its design is the reference the first coding slice ports onto the two-edge model: evidence is an authenticated logical read, not Merkle proof bytes; rejection and retraction both read the request's booked submission time; evidence binds the registry's abstract identity, the complete configuration including the intermediate root, and the complete request; an empty batch is refused; all-reject batches share the mixed-batch engine. The data model page names each of these; any difference from the earlier candidate is listed there.
